page.title: AI Workflow Consulting Guide for Marketing Teams
page.description: Learn what AI workflow consulting delivers, how to choose providers, tools, governance, and implementation steps for marketing operations.
page.h1: How should AI workflow consulting be run?
page.definition: AI workflow consulting is a structured engagement that assesses current processes, identifies high-impact use cases, selects appropriate tools, and builds a roadmap for human-in-the-loop automation across marketing, content, and event operations.
page.quick_answer: Start with a scoped assessment that maps your current workflow, prioritises use cases by effort and value, and defines a human-in-the-loop approval gate before any automation goes live.

sections.h2: What does an AI workflow consulting engagement deliver?

blocks.p: A consulting engagement delivers an assessment, a prioritised use-case list, a tool choice, and a roadmap with clear owners and approval gates.

ul: Current-state audit of content, event, and marketing operations
Ranked use cases scored by effort, value, and risk
Tool shortlist with integration mapping
Phased roadmap with milestones and owners
Governance model including human-in-the-loop rules

sections.h2: How do you choose between a consultant and an agency for AI workflows?

blocks.p: Consultants provide strategy and roadmap on a day rate or fixed project, while agencies build working automations, integrations, and documentation with a monthly retainer.

head: Factor
Consultant
Agency
rows: Assessment, use-case list, tool choice, roadmap
Fixed build fee plus monthly retainer

sections.h2: What tools and integrations are typically recommended for AI workflows?

blocks.p: Typical tool stacks combine work management, AI drafting, image generation, automation hand-offs, and reporting in a connected chain.

ul: Work management: Asana, Monday.com or ClickUp for the workflow
Research and drafts: ChatGPT or Claude
Image variants: Adobe Firefly or Canva
Hand-offs between apps: Zapier or Make
Reporting: HubSpot or GA4

sections.h2: How do you govern AI output with human-in-the-loop rules?

blocks.p: Every AI output remains a draft until a named person approves it, and each step in the workflow has an owner, an output, and an approval gate.

ol: Define Seven steps, each with an owner, an output and an approval gate
Assign a named approver for every AI-generated asset
Log prompt, model version, and output for audit trail
Set exception rate thresholds that trigger manual review
Schedule monthly governance review with stakeholders

sections.h2: What does implementation timeline and cost structure look like?

blocks.p: Engagements are scoped per project with consultants charging day rates or fixed fees and agencies charging a fixed build fee plus monthly retainer.

ul: Discovery and assessment: two to three weeks
Tool selection and pilot design: two weeks
Build and test first automation: three to four weeks
Rollout to additional use cases: phased over 90 days
Monthly retainer for optimisation and support

sections.h2: How do you measure success and iterate on AI workflows?

blocks.p: Success is measured by cycle time reduction, revision rounds, on-time rate, and capacity use, reviewed monthly over a 90-day initial plan.

ul: Cycle time from brief to publish
Revision rounds per asset
On-time delivery rate
Team capacity utilisation
Exception rate on AI-generated drafts

faq.q: What is the first deliverable I should expect from an AI workflow consultant?
faq.a: The first deliverable is a current-state assessment that maps your existing content, event, and marketing operations, identifies bottlenecks, and ranks use cases by effort, value, and risk before any tool is recommended.

faq.q: How do I know if my team needs a consultant or an agency?
faq.a: Choose a consultant when you need strategy, prioritisation, and a roadmap your team can execute. Choose an agency when you need working automations built, integrated, and maintained without adding internal engineering capacity.

faq.q: What governance rule prevents AI errors from reaching customers?
faq.a: The human-in-the-loop rule requires every AI output to remain a draft until a named person approves it. Each workflow step has an owner, an output, and an approval gate, with prompt logs and model versions recorded for audit.

faq.q: What metrics prove the workflow is improving over time?
faq.a: Track cycle time from brief to publish, revision rounds per asset, on-time delivery rate, team capacity utilisation, and exception rate on AI drafts. Review these monthly during the first 90 days to adjust the roadmap.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions offer general AI consulting?
faq.a: West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop AI workflows for marketing, content and event teams; it is not a general AI consultancy. Engagements are scoped per project; send the scope for a quote.
